creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`corpus/conformance/backend-intent.json` compares the driver's output to the case's `expect` as exact JSON, and the wire carries an f32. So a case written with `"amount": 0.05` fails against an actual of `0.05000000074505806`, and the only fractions expressible are the ones exactly representable in binary: 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625.

Found writing the resize-unit cases (a_29XVSQKAC), which now use 0.25 and 0.125 with a note saying why. That works and reads slightly wrong - the numbers are powers of two for a reason no reader of the case can see without the note, and herdr's own default step is 0.05, which the corpus cannot state.

The corpus is meant to be text a reviewer can read, so putting 0.05000000074505806 in the file is the wrong way out. The fix is on the comparison side: the driver should compare numbers at the width the wire carries rather than as decimal text. Worth checking whether any other case has quietly picked its numbers to dodge this - the split ratios are all 0.25/0.5/0.75, which may be taste or may be the same workaround.
title: 🔢 A corpus case cannot say 0.05
